title: Statutory & Regulatory Charges: STT, Stamp Duty, GST and SEBI Fees
content:
Regulatory and Statutory Levies on Indian Capital Market Transactions.

1. Securities Transaction Tax (STT):
STT is a mandatory central tax levied on the value of securities traded on recognized stock exchanges (NSE/BSE):
- Equity Delivery: 0.1% on both Buy and Sell sides of the trade value.
- Equity Intraday: 0.025% on the Sell side only (zero on Buy side).
- Equity Futures: 0.02% on the Sell side only.
- Equity Options: 0.1% on the Sell side (calculated on premium turnover), and 0.125% on intrinsic value for exercised options contracts.

2. Goods and Services Tax (GST):
A standardized GST rate of 18% is levied by the Government of India. GST is applicable on the sum of: (Brokerage + SEBI Turnover Charges + Exchange Transaction Charges + DP Charges). GST is never levied directly on the underlying stock value or STT.

3. Stamp Duty (Indian Stamp Act):
State stamp duty is collected centrally on purchase transactions only:
- Equity Delivery: 0.015% (Rs. 1,500 per crore) on Buy turnover.
- Equity Intraday: 0.003% (Rs. 300 per crore) on Buy turnover.
- Futures: 0.002% (Rs. 200 per crore) on Buy turnover.
- Options: 0.003% (Rs. 300 per crore) on Buy turnover.

4. SEBI Turnover Charges & Exchange Transaction Fees:
- SEBI Charges: Flat Rs. 10 per crore (0.0001%) across all segments for regulatory oversight.
- Exchange Transaction Fees: NSE charges 0.00297% on turnover; BSE charges 0.00375% on equity delivery turnover.
